title: Mulligatawny
subtitle: Spiced Anglo-Indian soup with lentils, apple, and coconut
excerpt: A fragrant, gently spiced soup of red lentils, apple, coconut milk, and chicken stock, thickened with lentils and finished with lemon. British-Indian in character, warming and deeply savoury.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mulligatawny is an Anglo-Indian soup created by British colonists in India who asked their Tamil cooks for a 'pepper water' (milagu tannir in Tamil) to serve as a first course in the British dining style. The result was a spiced broth that adapted elements of South Indian rasam and sambar to British taste. It arrived in Britain in the late 18th century and became a fixture of Victorian cookery. Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861) includes a recipe. The dish has evolved considerably from its Tamil origins, and the British version typically contains lentils, apple or another sweet element to balance the spice, and a coconut milk finish.

recipeTools.notes: And a stick blender for partial blending.

content.text: The apple adds a natural sweetness that balances the spice and the lemon at the end. Partially blend the soup rather than blending it completely: a little texture from the lentils and vegetables is part of the character of the dish. The soup thickens as it sits, so add a splash of water or stock when reheating.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan. Soften the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and spices. Cook for 1 minute, stirring.
Add the apple, lentils, and stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 25 minutes until the lentils are completely soft.
Partially blend: aim to leave some texture rather than a smooth puree. Stir in the coconut milk and lemon juice. Season with salt. Reheat gently. Serve topped with fresh coriander.
